blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a critical security threat posed by card skimmers, which are devices secretly attached to payment terminals to steal card data. He notes that traditional detection methods (like pulling on card readers or checking for unusual features) are ineffective against modern skimmers, which are often indistinguishable from legitimate devices. The paper introduces the Skim Reaper, a portable detection tool developed in collaboration with the NYPD Financial Crimes Task Force. The device leverages the fact that skimmers must physically read the magnetic stripe of a card, using a metallic read head. The Skim Reaper detects these read heads by measuring electrical contacts on a specially designed measurement card, reliably identifying 100% of tested skimmers, including those provided by law enforcement. The work underscores the growing threat of card skimming fraud and demonstrates a practical solution for consumers and law enforcement.
paper_title: Fear the reaper: characterization and fast detection of card skimmers
paper_abstract: Payment card fraud results in billions of dollars in losses annually. Adversaries increasingly acquire card data using skimmers, which are attached to legitimate payment devices including point of sale terminals, gas pumps, and ATMs. Detecting such devices can be difficult, and while many experts offer advice in doing so, there exists no large-scale characterization of skimmer technology to support such defenses. In this paper, we perform the first such study based on skimmers recovered by the NYPD’s Financial Crimes Task Force over a 16 month period. After systematizing these devices, we develop the Skim Reaper, a detector which takes advantage of the physical properties and constraints necessary for many skimmers to steal card data. Our analysis shows the Skim Reaper effectively detects 100% of devices supplied by the NYPD. In so doing, we provide the first robust and portable mechanism for detecting card skimmers.
